task.title: Meteosat and EPIC cloud-mask comparison quality anomaly
task.task: A completed remote-sensing comparison may contain a scientific silent failure. Use only public experiments to determine whether a fault exists and validate any repair.

hypotheses.description: The Meteosat and EPIC cloud masks are not spatially aligned (e.g., due to projection or geolocation errors), causing a systematic reduction in agreement.
testable_scope: spatial shift between the two masks
agreement improvement after applying small shifts

hypotheses.description: The two cloud masks are from different observation times, leading to genuine cloud movement and thus lower agreement.
testable_scope: time difference between the two datasets

hypotheses.description: The different spatial resolutions of Meteosat and EPIC cause cloud edge effects and partial cloud pixel classification differences, reducing agreement.
testable_scope: agreement improvement after resampling to common grid

hypotheses.description: The two cloud masks use different algorithms or thresholds, leading to systematic classification differences (e.g., thin cirrus detection).
The agreement of 0.537 is a scientifically valid result given the inherent differences between the two sensors and their cloud masks; no fault exists.
testable_scope: agreement is within expected range for such comparisons

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: If a spatial shift exists, agreement should improve for a specific (dr, dc) shift. Testing a small range of shifts provides direct evidence for or against H001.
experiments.predicted_observation: Agreement increases above 0.537 for some shift, or remains flat/declines, indicating no misalignment.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: Test H003 (sensor resolution difference) by resampling to a common grid and comparing agreement.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H003 is true, agreement will increase significantly (e.g., >0.6) after resampling; if false, agreement remains near 0.537.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: EXP_001 tested only a single (1,1) shift, which is insufficient to rule out spatial misalignment. A systematic sweep over a range of shifts will reveal whether any shift improves agreement, directly testing H001.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H001 is true, agreement_valid will increase above 0.537 for some (dr, dc) shift; if false, agreement remains near 0.537 for all shifts.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: EXP_001 and EXP_003 tested only two shifts; a systematic sweep over a range of shifts is needed to determine whether any shift improves agreement, directly testing H001.
experiments.predicted_observation: If H001 is true, agreement_valid will increase above 0.537 for some (dr, dc) shift; if false, agreement remains near 0.537 for all shifts.

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: Prior shift tests (EXP_001, EXP_003, EXP_004) show only tiny changes (max delta +0.00017), suggesting no large misalignment. However, only three shifts were tested. A systematic sweep over a wider range (dr, dc in [-5,5]) will map the agreement surface. If agreement remains near 0.537 for all shifts, H001 is strongly contradicted, and the low agreement is more likely due to temporal mismatch (H002) or algorithm differences (H004). If a shift yields a large improvement, H001 is supported.
experiments.predicted_observation: Agreement_valid remains within ±0.01 of 0.537 for all shifts, or a specific shift yields a substantial increase (e.g., >0.6).

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: Prior shift experiments (E001, E003, E004, E005) show agreement remains near 0.537 for all tested shifts (max delta +0.00017), strongly contradicting H001. The identity transform (E002) shows no change, and no resampling effect was tested. The remaining plausible causes are temporal mismatch (H002) and algorithm difference (H004). A confusion matrix can reveal systematic classification differences: if one mask consistently classifies more pixels as cloudy (e.g., thin cirrus detection), that supports H004; if the disagreement is spatially random, that supports H002. This is a low-cost, high-information experiment that has not been performed.
experiments.predicted_observation: Confusion matrix shows a systematic bias (e.g., one mask has much higher cloud fraction, or asymmetric false positive/negative rates), supporting H004; or shows balanced errors with no systematic bias, supporting H002.

experiments.predicted_observation: Agreement_valid remains within ±0.01 of 0.537 for all shifts, or a specific shift yields a substantial increase (e.g., >0.6).

experiments.diagnostic_rationale: H003 (sensor resolution difference) has not been properly tested. E002 used only an identity transform, which does not change resolution. A resampling operation (e.g., flip_x or rot90) would not change resolution either, but the transform_and_compare tool with a non-identity operation can reveal whether the comparison is sensitive to orientation/geometry, indirectly testing whether resolution/grid alignment matters. If agreement changes substantially, it suggests grid/projection issues (H003); if it remains near 0.537, H003 is less likely.
experiments.predicted_observation: Agreement_valid changes by more than 0.01 from 0.537 for some transform, supporting H003; or remains near 0.537, contradicting H003.

unresolved_questions: Is the 0.537 agreement within the expected range for Meteosat vs EPIC cloud-mask comparisons given inherent sensor and algorithm differences?
reflection.summary: All shift experiments (E001, E003, E004, E005, E007) show agreement remains within ±0.0005 of baseline, strongly contradicting spatial misalignment (H001). The rot90 transform (E008) reduced agreement to 0.477, indicating the comparison is sensitive to orientation but not to small shifts, which is inconsistent with a simple misalignment fault. No resampling to a common grid was performed, so H003 remains untested, but the lack of shift sensitivity and the large residual gap (0.213) suggest the low agreement is inherent. With budget exhausted and no evidence of a correctable fault, the scientifically valid conclusion is no_fault (H005).
